metadata.title: Two Early Warning Signs of a Recession
metadata.data_notes: The ICE high-yield spread is limited to 3 years on FRED, so the Moody's Baa spread (1986+) is used instead.

series_manifest.label: Corporate Borrowing Penalty (Baa Bond Yield minus 10-Yr Treasury)

events.label: Temp jobs start falling before the 2001 recession
Baa borrowing penalty spikes to 6.0 points
COVID: 920,000 temp jobs lost in one month

explanation.summary: Two warning signs of a recession. The first is the borrowing penalty: the extra interest that riskier companies pay compared with the US government. The second is the number of temp agency workers, often the first people companies let go. The stripes below show every month since 1998: red is a warning sign, blue is healthy. When the borrowing penalty rises, temp jobs tend to fall about 6 months later, and falling temp jobs come with recessions. The signs showed before the 2001 and 2008 recessions. COVID in 2020 came with almost no warning.
explanation.methodology: Borrowing penalty: Moody's Baa corporate bond yield minus the 10-year Treasury yield (FRED BAA10Y, monthly average). Temp jobs: BLS temporary help services employment (CES6056132001). Grey periods are official NBER recessions (FRED USREC). The high-yield spread used before is only available for 3 years on FRED, so the longer Baa spread replaces it.

key_findings.title: December 2008: Credit Freezes
key_findings.description: The Baa spread jumped to 6.0 percentage points, its highest on the chart. Temp jobs kept falling until June 2009, to 1.75 million, down a third from 2.6 million in late 2005.
key_findings.significance: When lenders panic, temp workers lose their jobs next.

key_findings.title: April 2020: Fastest Drop Ever
key_findings.description: Temp jobs fell from 2.87 million to 1.95 million in a single month as COVID closed businesses.
key_findings.significance: Temp staffing reacts within weeks to a sudden shock.

key_findings.title: March 2022 to Now: A Quiet Warning
key_findings.description: Temp jobs peaked at 3.16 million in March 2022. As of September 2026 they are 2.49 million, about 21% lower, even though there has been no recession and the borrowing penalty is low (1.5 points).
key_findings.significance: The two signals disagree today, which is unusual. Watch which one turns out right.
